# GpuFanController v1.7.2

This release makes controllers easier to identify in FanCtl and during firmware
updates. Give each controller a friendly name and select it from a numbered list;
there is no need to remember or copy its UUID. Nano firmware remains **1.7.0**.

## Highlights

- **Editable controller names:** Setup now has a Controller name field, saved
  through the existing Save changes review. Names are host-only labels; the
  permanent UUID, mappings and Nano calibration are unchanged. Unsaved edits
  survive navigation and Reload; invalid names remain drafts for correction.
- **Named firmware picker:** the installer delegates its optional Nano update to
  the installed updater. It lists cached controllers with name, USB port, firmware
  and shortened UUID. Select by number, or enter a port to look up its UUID.
- **Simpler confirmation:** review the selected controller and type `FLASH`.
  The updater still rechecks daemon UUID/port and the actual Nano identity before
  writing, backs up and verifies EEPROM, and validates settings after flashing.
- **Separate blank-board path:** unknown or unregistered devices are never
  assumed blank. First-time selection remains explicit and requires no Hello
  response plus fully erased EEPROM. No implicit USB scan or bulk flash is added.

## Compatibility

- Host: Ubuntu **24.04 amd64** with systemd; NVIDIA and experimental native-Linux
  AMD support are unchanged.
- Nano: classic ATmega328P, firmware **1.7.0**, protocol **2**, EEPROM schema **5**.
  There are no firmware source or EEPROM-layout changes.
- Controller names reuse the existing host configuration field: 1-64 printable
  ASCII characters, not blank. Duplicate names are allowed; UUID remains identity.
- No Nano reflash or recalibration is required. Existing mappings and settings
  are preserved. The explicit `--port`, `--controller-id`, `--bootloader` and
  `--uninitialized` paths remain available for advanced use.
- Host installation never flashes a Nano. `--yes` still confirms host installation
  only and skips the optional firmware question.

## Installation or upgrade

Download a fresh installer, inspect it, then run as your normal user:

```sh
curl --fail --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
  https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/releases/download/v1.7.2/install.py \
  --output gpu-fan-install.py
# Inspect gpu-fan-install.py before running it.
python3 gpu-fan-install.py --version 1.7.2 --start
```

The installer requests sudo for package/service operations. In FanCtl, edit
**Setup > Controller name**, then **Save changes**. For a separate supervised
firmware operation, use `sudo gpu-fan-controller-update-firmware --interactive`.
Missing controllers need the daemon running and an explicit FanCtl Scan USB /
Register Nano step; the picker itself never scans or resets ports.

See the [installation and firmware guide](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.2/docs/RELEASES.md)
and [FanCtl manual](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.2/docs/USER_MANUAL.md).

## Validation and limitations

- All **51 tests** passed locally, including **31 release-policy tests** and
  terminal coverage at 100x32 and 76x24. Coverage includes name persistence,
  invalid-name handling, save/discard behavior, duplicate names, manual-port
  lookup, cancellation, ambiguous inventory and changed device identity.
- The picker was exercised against the real Nano's cached metadata in WSL:
  numeric selection resolved its UUID and reached the `FLASH` prompt. Cancelling
  left the daemon running and performed no flash. This is separate from the
  successful 1.7.1 updater bench-flash test documented in the installation guide.
- Publication is gated on GitHub Actions host tests, firmware build, and isolated
  Ubuntu package install/reinstall/removal checks. This is not a cooling-under-load
  qualification or physical AMD validation; existing hardware limitations remain.
- Friendly names are stored by the daemon, not on the Nano, and do not travel
  with a board to another host unless the host configuration is transferred.

## Safety and support

Stop GPU workloads and supervise cooling during service interruptions, calibration
and flashing. This personal project is provided as is, without guarantees of
compatibility, cooling or reliability. Failures or incorrect wiring/settings can
damage hardware or cause data loss. Focused pull requests are welcome, but a
response, review or merge is not guaranteed. Issues and Discussions remain disabled.

See the [risk notice](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.2/README.md#use-at-your-own-risk),
[MIT license](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.2/LICENSE) and
[support policy](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.2/SUPPORT.md).
